title: Ten Times Bigger, Ten Times Smaller

steps.body: Multiplying by 10 shifts every digit one rung up the ladder — a new ones-slot opens at the end, filled with a zero. So **34 × 10 = 340**: the 3 and 4 both climbed one place, and a fresh 0 holds the emptied ones spot.
Match each number to ×10 of itself.

widget.prompt: Match each number to what it becomes when multiplied by 10.

pairErrors.feedback: 12,000 is 10 times 1,200, not 250. Shifting 250 one rung up gives 2,500.

widget.missFeedback: Shift every digit one place up, and fill the new ones-spot with a zero.

predict.prompt: Multiplying a whole number by 10 — do its digits CHANGE, or just SHIFT?

options.label: Shift — each digit moves one place left

predict.reveal: The digits keep their identities and slide one place up in rank — a zero fills the vacated ones place. ×10 is a promotion, not a rewrite.

explanationVariants: Each digit of 507 climbs one rung, and a new zero fills the ones spot: 5070.

commonErrors.feedback: 507 is unchanged — but ×10 shifts every digit one rung up. 507 becomes 5,070.
5007 inserted the zero in the middle. The new zero always fills the fresh ONES spot at the end: 5,070.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Shift every digit of 507 one place up, and open a new ones-slot with a 0.

steps.body: Dividing by 10 undoes the shift: every digit moves one rung DOWN, and the last zero disappears. **4,800 ÷ 10 = 480** — each digit dropped a rung, and the ones-place zero vanished with it.

explanationVariants: Removing the last zero and sliding every digit down gives 480.

commonErrors.feedback: 48 shifted TWO rungs down instead of one — that's ÷100. Dividing by 10 only drops one rung: 480.
4810 added instead of removed a digit. Dividing by 10 removes the last zero and shifts down: 480.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Drop every digit of 4,800 one rung down, removing the last zero.

widget.prompt: Match each division by 10 to its result.

pairErrors.feedback: 76 is 760 ÷ 10. Shifting 9,300 down one rung and dropping its zero gives 930.

widget.missFeedback: Drop every digit one rung, removing the last zero.
widget.successFeedback: 760→76, 9,300→930, 150→15 — every digit dropped exactly one rung.

steps.body: Ten times as many, for real.
explanationVariants: Every digit of 630 climbs one place: 6,300.

widget.prompt: A factory made 630 toys this year. Next year it plans to make 10 TIMES as many. How many toys is that?

commonErrors.feedback: 640 added 10 instead of multiplying by 10. Shifting every digit of 630 one rung up gives 6,300.
63,000 shifted TWO rungs — that's ×100. Ten times shifts only one rung: 6,300.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Shift every digit of 630 one rung up.

hints: Now multiply that result by 10 again.

widget.prompt: Start with 25. Multiply by 10, then multiply that result by 10 again. What number do you reach?

commonErrors.feedback: 250 is only ONE shift (25 × 10). The problem asks for two shifts: 250 × 10 = 2,500.
That's four extra rungs too many. Two ×10 shifts from 25 reach 2,500, not further.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Shift 25 up one rung, then shift that result up one more rung.

takeaways: ×10 shifts every digit one rung up; a new zero fills the ones-spot.
÷10 shifts every digit one rung down, removing the last zero.
Repeated shifts climb multiple rungs — two ×10s reach two rungs higher.
steps.teaser: next: naming every place from ones all the way up to the millions.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **×10 shifts every digit one rung up and opens a new zero at the end.** For 12 × 10: the 1 and 2 both climb one place, and a zero fills the fresh ones-spot: 120.

explanationVariants: ×10 opens a new zero at the end: 120.

options.feedback: Every digit shifts one rung up, with a new zero at the end: 120.
22 added 10 instead of multiplying. ×10 shifts digits up: 12 becomes 120.
1200 shifted two rungs — that's ×100. One rung (×10) gives 120.
